utility.notes: SCE's own 'Incorporated Cities and Counties Served by SCE' fact sheet (updated 3/17/2025) explicitly lists 'La Habra' by name among the cities in its service area.

generation_supplier.notes: Orange County Power Authority (OCPA), the CCA operating in Orange County, currently names Buena Park, Fullerton, Irvine, and Fountain Valley as members — La Habra was not named among current members this session. Left null rather than asserted either way.

county.notes: La Habra is a well-documented Orange County city; also listed under Orange County in SCE's own service-area fact sheet.

permit_authority.value: City of La Habra Building and Safety Division

interconnection_url.notes: SCE's own Net Energy Metering (NEM) program page — a utility-wide fact already established for other SCE-territory records this session.

value.name: SGIP - Residential Solar and Storage Equity
value.administrator: Southern California Edison (SCE), under the CPUC's Self-Generation Incentive Program
value.description: Storage incentive of $1,100/kWh paired with a solar incentive of $3,100/kW, funded via a $280 million CPUC-authorized budget that opened for reservations June 2, 2025. Administered by SCE across its entire distribution territory, which includes La Habra/Orange County.
value.eligibility: PG&E or SCE residential customers (general market tier)

battery_programs.notes: Same statewide CPUC-administered SGIP program already confirmed for other SCE-territory records this session, reused as a utility-level fact.

value.name: Eligibility checklist for expedited permitting (Toolkit Document 2)
Standard Electrical Plan (Toolkit Document 3 or 4, for systems 10kW or less) or a full electrical plan with equipment cut sheets, labeling, and site diagram
Roof plan showing layout, PV panels, and fire safety items (access point, access pathways, fire classification, required labels/markings)

Expedited Structural Criteria (Toolkit Document 5) for qualifying systems, or full structural drawings/calculations stamped by a California-licensed Civil or Structural Engineer for non-qualifying systems

value: Schedule on-site inspection by calling Building and Safety at 562-383-4116
Inspection requests received by 4:00pm are typically scheduled for the next business day; if unavailable, inspection occurs as soon as possible
Approved plans must be on the job site and accessible to the inspector, or a re-inspection fee applies

value.notes: Per the city's own Submittal Requirements Bulletin (Rev. 01/26): 'Permit applications should be reviewed in three working days.'

value.program_or_pathway: Streamlined permitting for solar PV installations 10kW or less in one- and two-family dwellings
other_conditions: Only a Combination Building/Electrical permit is required for systems 10kW or less; Planning Department and Fire Department approval is not required at this size

value.name: Standard-plan solar photovoltaic permit fee
value.notes: Per the city's own bulletin: 'Fees will not exceed $500.00 for systems utilizing the standard plan.' Plan check fee is hourly (1-hour minimum) if a standard plan is not used; permit fees for non-standard-plan systems are based on construction valuation. Electrical permits apply only if an electrical panel upgrade is proposed (separate permit). Strong Motion Tax and CBSC fees also apply. Re-inspection fees apply if more than one inspection is required.

value.role: City of La Habra Building and Safety
